headline: New evening confusion since about mid-October, including the stove left on once, comes with caregiver exhaustion and a request for respite. No result from the planned workup is documented.

items.statement: On 2026-11-02 his grandson Robert reported about two weeks of increased evening confusion, with the stove left on once. Jerónimo was oriented to person and place but not date, with no fever. The nurse planned a urinalysis, medication review and PCP visit that week. No results or visit are documented in the provided notes, and the encounters record is empty.
items.verifier_note: All details match the 2026-11-02 nursing note. The empty encounters record supports the statement that no visit is documented.

items.statement: On 2026-11-22 Robert, his primary caregiver, reported exhaustion and poor sleep. He is worried about managing evenings alone and requested respite. The social worker discussed respite options and a caregiver support group.
items.verifier_note: The 2026-11-22 social work note matches every detail in the statement.

items.statement: The PT evaluation on 2026-09-29 found slow, unsteady gait with intermittent cane use and a Timed Up and Go of 19 seconds. PT recommended a front-wheeled walker, a home safety evaluation and bathroom grab bars, with PT twice weekly for strength and balance. The notes do not show whether these were put in place.
items.verifier_note: The PT evaluation note matches every detail, including the gait findings, the TUG of 19 seconds, the recommendations, and PT twice weekly. The statement says the notes don't show whether the recommendations were put in place, and the cited note doesn't say either.

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and that the prior IDT review date is documented so changes are measured from the correct baseline.

Falls and near-falls since last review: count, circumstances, injuries, and whether any fall occurred while on new cardiac medications; note osteoporosis on alendronic acid raises fracture-risk stakes.

ED visits and hospital admissions in the window, especially any chest pain, cardiac, or bleeding-related presentations given new ischemic heart disease diagnosis (onset 2026-06-30) and recent cardiac medication starts.
Cardiac symptom review: chest pain or angina frequency, nitroglycerin spray use (new 2026-07-07), dyspnea, dizziness, palpitations; check whether PRN nitroglycerin use has increased.

Medication start/stop review since last review: metoprolol succinate, clopidogrel, simvastatin, nitroglycerin, alendronic acid started in mid-2026; confirm adherence, refills, and any dose changes or discontinuations.

Bleeding and antiplatelet safety: any bruising, GI bleeding signs, dental bleeding (history of impacted molars), or hematuria while on clopidogrel; coordinate with the prescriber on any planned dental procedures.
Blood pressure and heart rate trend in the window, including orthostatic readings given beta-blocker start and fall history; flag bradycardia or hypotension.
Weight trend and BMI (obesity on record since 1990); note any weight change relevant to cardiac status and statin/beta-blocker tolerance.

Pain and migraine status: chronic pain and chronic intractable migraine frequency, severity, and analgesic use; check for medication overuse or new analgesic prescriptions, and whether any pain medication interacts with the cardiac regimen.

Substance use review given dependent drug abuse (onset 2018): any relapse signals, opioid or sedative use, pharmacy refill patterns, urine screen or counseling notes, and whether any controlled substances were prescribed in the window; check for safety implications with metoprolol and nitroglycerin.
Function and ADLs/IADLs: mobility given scoliosis and osteoporosis, transfers, self-care, medication management ability, and any change since last review.
Cognition and mood screening: any new cognitive concerns, depression or anxiety screen results, and attendance at PACE day services or appointments in the window.
Caregiver and social situation: living arrangement, caregiver availability or strain, transportation, and any changes in support since last review.

Care-plan items due: cardiology or cardiac follow-up, lipid panel and statin monitoring, bone density or osteoporosis follow-up for alendronic acid, pain and migraine care-plan review, substance use treatment plan review, and any overdue assessments (MDS/care plan review dates).
